subject: Quick console help text: subprocessors & transfers — Acme review
messages:
From: Annette Cho <acme-legal@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Help text for console — subprocessors & transfers

Hi Karthik,

We're finalizing procurement for Acme Cloud's teams and procurement asked for a short, clear blurb we can link to from our security questionnaire that explains: (1) how Redwood uses subprocessors, (2) where data may be transferred internationally for hosted API customers, and (3) whether customers can choose data residency.

Can you share a one-sentence + one-paragraph "QuickCard" (console help tooltip length) that we can include in our RFP appendix? The current DPA is fine but procurement needs a plain-language line they can paste into their internal docs.

Attached is a short list of questions from our procurement lead (Acme_DPA_Qs.pdf). Please cc your legal and product folks.

Thanks —
Annette Cho
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloud
acme-legal@acme.com

--attachment: Acme_DPA_Qs.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Annette Cho <acme-legal@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Help text for console — subprocessors & transfers

Annette — thanks for the prompt. Looping in Laura and Marissa for legal language and Jordan for console placement.

Draft options below — both intended to be short (tooltip + one-sentence detail) so procurement can paste easily. Can legal flag any problematic claims (e.g., "we anonymize" or absolute guarantees)? Also, do you want the snippet to reference the full DPA URL or a shorter link to the subprocessor list?

Option A (very short):
"Redwood uses vetted subprocessors to operate and secure our hosted API; data may be processed across regions — see our DPA and subprocessor list for details, and use the residency toggle to keep data in your preferred region when available."

Option B (slightly expanded):
"We engage subprocessors for infrastructure and monitoring. Some hosted requests may be routed to data centers outside your region; customers with residency requirements can opt into regional hosting in the Console (see Residency settings). Our DPA and up-to-date subprocessor list describe contractual safeguards and transfer mechanisms."

Attached is a plain-text file with both options and a suggested link target: https://redwood.ai/legal/dpa and https://redwood.ai/trust/subprocessors.

If this looks reasonable, I'll iterate with legal and send back one canonical QuickCard.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

--attachment: console_quickcard_v1.txt (text)

Karthik — quick edits from a product + privacy clarity perspective. I prefer Option B with tightened phrases below (I've marked changes inline):

Suggested canonical QuickCard (short tooltip title + 1-sentence body):
Title (tooltip): "Subprocessors & cross-border transfers"
Body: "Redwood may engage subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, logging and monitoring services) to operate the hosted API. Some hosted requests may be processed in other countries; customers with residency requirements can enable the Console’s Residency setting to keep data in a specific region when available. See our DPA and the live subprocessor list for contractual protections and transfer mechanisms."

Notes:
- Replace "infrastructure and monitoring" with examples to be explicit but not exhaustive.
- "When available" hedges on region availability to avoid promise of infinite capacity.
- We should include an explicit link for the live subprocessor list — that is what procurement will check.

I attached a redline for wording tweaks. If Marissa approves legal phrasing, Jordan can queue this in the help text carousel.

Laura Bennett
Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

--attachment: redline_quickcard_v2.txt (text)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Help text for console — subprocessors & transfers

Thanks — this is close. A couple of legal polish points before we ship externally to Acme: 

1) Remove any language that could be read as an absolute operational guarantee (e.g., "keep data in a specific region" → change to "keep data in a specific region where Redwood offers residency for your account").
2) Add a parenthetical noting that the DPA includes transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent) where relevant.
3) Do not use the word "anonymize" or imply irreversible de-identification unless we can prove it in our controls — not present in the draft but watch for future edits.

Final legal-approved copy suggestion (for customer-facing QuickCard):
Title: "Subprocessors & cross-border transfers"
Body: "Redwood may engage subprocessors (for example: cloud infrastructure, logging, and monitoring). Some hosted requests may be processed outside your region; accounts eligible for regional hosting can enable the Console’s Residency setting to keep data in a region where Redwood offers residency for that account. See our DPA (which describes transfer safeguards such as SCCs) and the live subprocessor list for details."

If that's acceptable, I approve sending to Acme. Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Annette / Tom — thanks for the patience. Per legal and product review, here's a concise QuickCard we recommend for the Console and procurement materials. This is the canonical text we can ship into the tooltip and include in the RFP appendix.

Title: Subprocessors & cross-border transfers

Body: Redwood may engage subprocessors (for example: cloud infrastructure, logging, and monitoring). Some hosted requests may be processed outside your region; accounts eligible for regional hosting can enable the Console’s Residency setting to keep data in a region where Redwood offers residency for that account. See our DPA (which describes transfer safeguards such as SCCs) and the live subprocessor list for details.

Links:
- DPA (full text): https://redwood.ai/legal/dpa
- Live subprocessor list: https://redwood.ai/trust/subprocessors
- Residency settings doc (Console): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-residency-guide

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Qs.pdf (your original questions) — I attached our suggested text as a plain .txt in case procurement wants it copy/paste-ready.

If this works, please confirm and we'll mark the QuickCard as "approved for Acme" and Jordan will schedule the Console update. If you need a shorter one-line variant for a spreadsheet, say the word and we'll provide a 140-character line.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
